newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN SHARES EASE AS LOCAL SUPPORT COOLS. [CORRECTED 11:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN SHARES EASE AS LOCAL SUPPORT COOLS. [CORRECTED 11:05 GMT]

text.p: Leading Russian shares were little changed in midday trade on Thursday, although traders saw the market trending lower overall as Russian investors started to leave for the summer.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index opened a hair lower than Wednesday's close, at 551.79 after 552.62.

Creditanstalt Grant senior trader Andrei Galperin saw upward pressure in prices to the end of the week due to shortcovering and money still washing around on the market, but said liquid shares were due to come off a little based on previous behaviour.
"The blue chips are overheated, the last time they took off there was a slight price imbalance and they became more expensive than (less liquid) shares," said Galperin.
National power company UES rose to $0.4435 at 1015 GMT after closing on Wednesday at $0.4385. But regional utility Mosenergo was unchanged at $1.710 while Rostelekom ticked up to $4.77 from $4.76.
Prospekt's head of equity trading Andrei Ippolitov saw the market settling lower on the back of the Dow Jones index, which closed lower on Wednesday at 7928.32.
"There are objective reasons, but the Dow Jones is more of an emotional reason," Creditanstalt Grant's Galperin said (corrects from Ippolitov).

He saw aggressive Russian clients, focused up to now on government securities but who have kept the market buoyant in recent days as Western interest tailed off, taking a more measured approach to equities.
"I think Russian banks are beginning to see that they're not so good at playing and are starting to work through brokerages," said Galperin, seeing the market quieting down by next month.
"The pressure on the market is already becoming more reserved and less aggressive."
